---
title: "QGIS"
subtitle: "Adding the regions to QGIS, with their colours and labels"
---

## Add the layer from a URL

In QGIS, **Layer ▸ Add Layer ▸ Add Vector Layer…**, choose **Protocol: HTTP(S), cloud, etc.**, and
enter a URL:

```
https://australianantarcticdivision.github.io/measoshapes/data/v06/measo_regions06.fgb
```

Use FlatGeobuf (`.fgb`), which every recent QGIS can read. GeoParquet (`.parquet`) works if your QGIS
build includes the GDAL Parquet driver (check **Settings ▸ Options ▸ GDAL ▸ Vector Drivers**). You can
also download a file from the [Data](data.qmd) page and drag it onto the map.

Which file:

* `measo_regions06.fgb`: polar equal area, for maps of the Southern Ocean and areas.
* `measo_regions06_epsg_3031.fgb`: polar stereographic (EPSG:3031), to match
  [Quantarctica](https://www.npolar.no/quantarctica/) and other EPSG:3031 data.
* `measo_regions06_ll.fgb`: longitude/latitude.

QGIS reprojects layers on the fly, so any of them can be shown in a project in another projection.

## Colours and labels

Download the style [measo_regions06.qml](data/v06/measo_regions06.qml), then in the layer's
**Properties ▸ Symbology**, choose **Style ▸ Load Style…** and select the file. The regions are
categorized by `name` with the fill colours and legend labels such as "Antarctic Atlantic (AOA)"; the
T regions (outside MEASO) are outlined only.

Alternatively, use the `fill` column directly: in **Symbology**, set the fill colour to
*Data defined override ▸ Edit…* with the expression

```
coalesce("fill", '#00000000')
```

and use `label` for labels.

## From the Python console

```python
base = "https://australianantarcticdivision.github.io/measoshapes/data/v06"
layer = iface.addVectorLayer(f"/vsicurl/{base}/measo_regions06.fgb", "MEASO regions", "ogr")

import urllib.request, tempfile, os
qml = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "measo_regions06.qml")
urllib.request.urlretrieve(f"{base}/measo_regions06.qml", qml)
layer.loadNamedStyle(qml)
layer.triggerRepaint()
```
